In today’s episode, we sit down with Annie Jacobsen - investigative journalist and bestselling author who has spent her career inside the world of nuclear weapons, Area 51 and national security.

We discuss what really happens in the first minutes of a nuclear war - why it’s measured in seconds, why it can’t be stopped, and what a single bomb does to a city. Annie walks us through the chilling math of 12,500 warheads and a 26-minute war, the truth behind Area 51 and why the government let the UFO myth grow, and how, as a reporter, she pries the world’s most guarded secrets out of the dark.

Gripping, sobering and impossible to look away from this one will change how you see the world you live in.

In today’s episode, we sit down with Dr Arunabha Ghosh, Climate & Energy Policy Expert | Former CEO, CEEW, to understand the economics of climate change and the future of energy in India.

We discuss why India is facing rising heat stress, how extreme weather affects jobs, agriculture and economic growth, and why climate change is no longer just an environmental issue. Arunabha explains how air pollution impacts productivity and foreign investment, why global energy systems remain vulnerable to oil shocks, and how India can reduce its dependence on fossil fuels.

The conversation also covers opportunities in climate tech, including battery recycling, rooftop solar, bamboo and green hydrogen. Arunabha shares practical ways to keep homes cooler without relying entirely on air conditioning, and explains how better urban planning and clean energy can shape India's future.

In today's episode, we sit down with Robert J. O'Neill former SEAL Team Six operator, bestselling author, and the man who fired the shots that killed Osama bin Laden for an unforgettable conversation about fear, courage and the mindset that never quits.

Robert takes us inside the one-way mission: the goodbye letters he wrote to his daughters, the two helicopters with no backup, and what really happened on the night that changed history. Raw, intense and deeply inspiring this one will change how you face your hardest moments.

We discuss why he stopped after running over 620 km in a Backyard Ultra, how he trained his mind to tolerate extreme pain, and what he learned from David Goggins about discipline, mental toughness, and pushing beyond his limits. The conversation also explores how he deals with the urge to quit, why he focuses on one loop at a time instead of the total distance, how visualization helped shape his ambitions, and his practical advice for anyone looking to build mental strength, get out of their comfort zone, and change their life.

In today’s episode, we sit down with Barbara Butcher, a retired death investigator from the NYC Office of Chief Medical Examiner who investigated over 5,500 deaths, including homicides, suicides, accidents and disasters, across two decades.

We talk about what Barbara looks for in the first moments at a death scene, why nobody can tell the exact time of death, and what happens to the body after we die. She shares how she reads gunshot wounds, blood spatter, and ligature marks, and how killers stage murders to look like suicides.

We also talk about the real reasons people kill, why so many murders in America go unsolved, and the booby-trapped suicide scene that almost cost her life. She reveals the emotional weight of working through the aftermath of 9/11, the personal toll of shutting down her feelings, and what the dead teach us about living with gratitude.
